WebRTC RFC 8839 / RFC 8863 SDP ICE: Candidate Port-Scan SSRF, remote-candidates & Ta Pacing
P965 [1024, 65535] Candidate Port & Completed-Only remote-candidates Gate · P966 🎉 [20, 500]ms Ta Pacing & [1, 4] Backup Pairs
❌ Unprotected RFC 8839 / RFC 8863 ICE Vulnerabilities
1. Privileged Port (<1024) STUN SSRF & Initial remote-candidates
• Malicious SDP injects a=candidate with port 22/53/6379 or IMDS IP
• Turns SFU into internal STUN port scanner & SSRF reflector
• Premature a=remote-candidates in initial Offer bypasses STUN check
2. Unpaced Continual Nomination (Ta < 20ms) & Backup Pair Storm
• Continual nomination probes 32 backup candidate pairs at Ta=1ms
• STUN Binding flood consumes >90 kbps on weak 5G/LTE uplink
• Starves 20ms Opus voice frames during Wi-Fi → cellular handoff
Enterprise Production Impact (Without P965–P966)
• Internal Redis/DB ports probed via STUN Binding packets
• Mobile roaming triggers uplink congestion & robotic voice
Verdict: BLOCK (Candidate Port-Scan SSRF / STUN Ta Flood)
✅ Deterministic SDP ICE & Continual Nomination Guards (P965–P966 🎉)
P965: [1024, 65535] Candidate Port & remote-candidates State Gate
• Reject a=candidate ports <1024 & RFC 1918 / loopback / IMDS IPs
• Allow a=remote-candidates only in re-Offers after ICE Completed
• Clamp candidate port range strictly within [1024, 65535]
• privilegedOrPrematureRemoteCandidateViolations == 0
• Gate: evaluateWebrtcSdpRfc8839IceCandidatePortRangeAndRemote...()
P966 🎉 (975th Guard / 130th SVG): Ta [20,500]ms & [1,4] Backup Pairs
• Clamp ICE STUN pacing timer Ta within [20, 500]ms (RFC 8445 §14.2)
• Cap active continual-nomination backup pairs to [1, 4] per stream
• Pre-warm 5G backup pair with <3 kbps overhead & 0ms switchover
• unpacedStunFloodOrBackupPairOverflowDrops == 0
• Gate: evaluateWebrtcRfc8863IceContinualNominationTaPacing...()
Verdict: PASS (0 Candidate SSRF · Paced Ta=[20,500]ms · 928 Tests)
